processing: Certified organic Darjeeling tea. Besides ordinary leaf, the estate hand-ties specialty teas such as peony rosettes and florettes that open like a flower in hot water.
harvest_season: As with other Darjeeling gardens, first flush in early spring and second flush in early summer are the most prized.
appearance_dry: Twisted Darjeeling leaf for standard lots; the specialty teas are hand-tied rosettes.
appearance_liquor: Pale gold to amber by flush, as is typical of Darjeeling.
appearance_wet: Green and coppery leaf; florettes open into a flower shape.
taste_profile: Little is recorded about this garden's taste. As with other Darjeelings, expect floral notes in spring and rounder fruit in summer.

brewing.notes: Western-style. Brew a florette in a tall glass, one per pot, and give it time to open.

vintage_note: Sold by year and flush as is usual for Darjeeling, and best within a year or two. Hand-tied florettes are specialty items and are slow to make, so expect small quantities.
description:
Avongrove is an organic estate in the Rangbhang Valley, on the banks of the Balason River in the Mirik area. It stretches from 670 metres at the river to 1,700 metres, a wide range that means no single altitude story fits all of its tea.

Its curiosity is hand-made display tea. A worker making florettes, which open into a flower when steeped, can make only six in a day. They are a pleasure to watch, and you pay for the handwork more than for the flavour.

For regular leaf, follow normal Darjeeling practice: cooler water in spring, a bit more heat and time in summer. Florettes want a tall glass so they can open.

The estate is certified organic under US, Japanese and Indian schemes. Ask which flush and which part of the garden a lot comes from if the seller knows.
history: Little is documented about the founding of the garden. About 200 hectares grow tea, and 500 workers live on the estate. The name is said to mean Nest of Birds.
